methodology.codexInstall: Install all 13 skills with skills@1.5.22 --copy into an isolated temporary Git project, then compare every installed SKILL.md byte-for-byte with the current repository; hash the existing global skill files before and after to prove they were not changed
methodology.activation: Requires a recorded task-level run; discovery or installation alone is not activation evidence
methodology.claudeCodeObservation: Claude Code invokes skills by name through a tool, so the model that chooses the skill is the same model that writes the task wording and judges the result. Session-list discovery and skill loading are directly observable and recorded; auto-activation is NOT recorded, because a self-test is not equivalent evidence to the Codex round, where the client named the skill unprompted.

clients.claudeCode: Claude Code (Claude Agent SDK session, model claude-opus-5)

codexInstall.note: All 13 current repository SKILL.md files matched the isolated installed copies byte-for-byte. This verifies the recorded project-copy install only; it does not prove activation or future versions.

projectUpdate.note: A controlled historical fixture replaced all 13 project copies while preserving the generated lock file. Project update restored all complete skill folders to the then-current public repository content. This does not verify global updates, lockless installs, activation, or future CLI versions.

existingGlobalCopies.note: The existing global copies were installed before later repository metadata and content updates. Installation is not continuous synchronization; update or reinstall before assuming the local copy matches the current repository.

codexActivation.note: All 13 skills automatically activated in one task. Ten tasks completed in the recorded run, one correctly paused for required user input, and two large tasks initially did not complete before passing smaller bounded retests. This is not evidence for every prompt or client version

prospectiveRetests.note: All six preregistered tasks were executed in isolated single-skill projects. Four passed all checks; two passed three of four and are retained as failures. This does not change the earlier 13-skill activation outcome totals.

remediationRetests.note: Both initially failed tasks were rerun with the exact original prompts after targeted Skill instruction fixes. Both passed 4/4; initial 3/4 failures remain preserved.

claudeCode.note: Discovery and loading are directly observable: 13/13 appeared in the session skill list and loaded with a correctly resolved base directory. Task coverage was judged from output content: first round 12/13 completed, guofeng-threejs partial because the installed copy predated a corrected technique (the stale copy still recommends Sobel post-processing for gongbi outlines, which this repository replaced with inverted-hull after measuring that fwidth(N) crease detection fails on smooth organic shapes). Auto-activation is deliberately NOT claimed: the same model chose the skill, wrote the wording and judged the result. Single run, single wording, single model version. On 2026-08-28 the local copies were brought to parity and all seven drifted skills were re-run against current content: 13/13 completed. Retesting in the same session was possible because SKILL.md bodies are read from disk at invocation time; only descriptions are loaded at session start.

discoveryContextBudget.note: Codex reported that some skill descriptions were shortened to fit the skills context budget

globalUpdate.remediation: npx skills@1.5.23 add <repo> --skill <name> -g, one skill at a time
globalUpdate.note: update -g only processes skills that have an entry in the global lock file. Seven skills installed on 2026-08-08 had no entry, were silently skipped for 20 days, and the command still exited 0 reporting success. This round did NOT verify whether a skill that HAS a lock entry updates correctly when upstream moves ahead: all six locked skills were already current, so that path was never exercised.
